This capability is available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions at no additional cost. To learn more, see Interface VPC endpoints in the IAM Identity Center User Guide. For more information, visit the IAM Identity Center product page .

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports KV cache-aware routing for real-time inference endpoints
items.description: Amazon SageMaker AI now supports KV cache-aware routing for real-time inference endpoints, enabling you to reduce time to first token for LLM workloads with long or repeated prompts. Serving engines such as vLLM store the computed key-value (KV) cache for repeated prompt starts such as shared system prompts, documents, and conversation history, to skip repeated work. Across several instances, a request that lands where the cache is missing recomputes it. Under high load, instances also evict cached blocks to free GPU memory, including shared prompts and earlier conversation turns. KV cache-aware routing sends each request to the instance that holds the longest matching part of its prompt in cache. The vLLM container reports the cache blocks it stores and evicts, and SageMaker routes with that live view. If the lookup is slow or finds no match, the endpoint falls back to load-aware routing, so the request is still served. Prefix-aware routing suits stable shared prompts, short prompts, or moderate load. KV cache-aware routing suits long prompts, high load, and limited GPU memory. Customers can now enable this feature by setting `RoutingStrategy` to `KV_AWARE` on a production variant and adding one environment variable so the container reports cache events. Customer can invoke the endpoint with the same APIs and OpenAI-compatible payloads. It supports single-model endpoints and inference components, including LoRA adapters, on GPU instances. It requires the AWS vLLM Deep Learning Container version 0.33.0 or later with at least two instances or inference component copies. Detailed observability metrics show KV cache hit rate. There is no additional charge for KV cache-aware routing. KV cache-aware routing is available today in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker AI is available. To get started, update to the latest AWS SDK or CLI. To learn more, visit the Amazon SageMaker AI inference page and see the API documentation .

items.title: AWS Network Firewall now supports context-aware rules with AWS Transit Gateway-attached firewalls
items.description: AWS Network Firewall attached to AWS Transit Gateway now allows you to use context-aware rules in your firewall policy. Network Firewall is a managed firewall and intrusion prevention service that inspects and filters traffic across your virtual private clouds (VPCs). With context-aware rules, you write rules that reference context from VPC resources instead of IP addresses. This makes it easier to apply consistent security controls as your organization grows. Existing rules automatically cover new workloads, so you don't need to update rules manually. Context-aware rules match traffic using VPCs, subnets, security groups, and Transit Gateway attachment identifiers, collectively known as context identifiers. You can reference context identifiers in a rule's source for any protocol, and in its destination for TCP-based protocols such as HTTP, TLS, and SSH. Flow and alert logs include context identifiers, so you can investigate activity based on context. Context-aware rules are available at no additional charge in all commercial and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. For a full list of supported Regions, see the AWS Capabilities by Region page . To learn more, see the AWS Network Firewall product page and documentation .

items.title: AWS Security Hub now detects when vulnerable software is running on Amazon EC2 instances
items.description: AWS Security Hub now detects when software with a known vulnerability is actively running on your Amazon EC2 instances. Exposure findings now include a new trait, *The EC2 instance is running software with a known vulnerability*. These findings get a higher severity rating than findings for the same vulnerability where the software isn't running. This helps your security team focus on the vulnerabilities that pose the greatest risk, without investing time and resources to investigate if the software is actually in use. Security teams managing thousands of instances can now prioritize patching based on actual runtime risk.  Security Hub correlates data from Amazon GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring and Amazon Inspector VM Scanner to detect running vulnerable software. It then combines this with other signals to generate exposure findings for EC2 resources that may be at risk, so you can prioritize response and remediation. This capability is available at no additional cost with the AWS Security Hub Essentials plan in all AWS Regions where Security Hub is available . To learn more, see the AWS Security Hub User Guide , the exposure definition in Remediating exposures for EC2 , the AWS Security Hub product page , the GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring User Guide , and the Amazon Inspector VM Scanner User Guide . For the full list of Regions, see the AWS Regional Services List .
